claim.quote: The results indicate strange quark contributions of < 10% of the charge and magnetic nucleon form factors at these four-momentum transfers.

key_value_text.quote: We have measured parity-violating asymmetries in elastic electron-proton and quasi-elastic electron-deuteron scattering at Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2.
key_value_text.value: Asymmetries on hydrogen and deuterium at Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2

name: G0 backward angle: strange-quark contributions below 10% at Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2

summary.plain: With its detectors turned to catch backward-scattered electrons, G0 measured asymmetries on hydrogen and deuterium at two momentum transfers. Combined with the forward data they show strange quarks contribute under ten percent of the nucleon's charge and magnetic form factors.
summary.technical: Parity-violating asymmetries in elastic e-p and quasi-elastic e-d scattering at Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2 (359 and 684 MeV beams); strange-quark contributions < 10% of the charge and magnetic form factors, and the first measurement of anapole effects in the axial current at these momentum transfers.

title: Strange Quark Contributions to Parity-Violating Asymmetries in the Backward Angle G0 Electron Scattering Experiment
why_it_matters: Separated the strange electric and magnetic form factors, and the axial form factor, at two momentum transfers in one experiment.
